chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who performed Sa'ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa for eight circuits, what is upon him? He said: 'If it was a mistake, one is dropped, and he counts with seven.'

key_terms.اطَّرَحَ: Dropped or discarded (referring to the extra circuit)
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which Sa'ee is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, the second hill in the Sa'ee ritual

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performs eight circuits of Sa'ee instead of seven?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility in the ritual of Sa'ee, demonstrating the Shia juristic principle that unintentional errors do not invalidate the core obligation. It highlights the practical application of 'ease in religion' by allowing the pilgrim to count seven circuits as sufficient when the eighth was performed inadvertently, reflecting the broader theological emphasis on divine mercy in ritual jurisprudence.
